strengths: Opens inside a platform scene (marks, alighting, files) instead of a generic ‘visitors notice’ template
Answers why to keep reading in the intro: practical habit, not national magic, and it also breaks
Visitor tips are concrete and ordered by usefulness (floor first, let people off, repair by going to the end)
FAQ matches real searcher questions (patience, painted lines, no obvious line, phones, cutting, elevators)
Aha is clear: waiting as infrastructure / traffic engineering for bodies, not a personality

issues.problem: ‘Loop-line station’ is insider transit jargon; many first-time readers will not map it to a Yamanote-style circle line.
issues.suggestion: Say ‘a busy city loop line’ or ‘a packed urban platform’ without requiring local network knowledge.

issues.problem: Number tickets, rainy geometry, and alighting-before-boarding recur across body, scenarios, tips, and FAQ. Useful, but the middle can feel like the same lesson restated.
issues.suggestion: Keep one authoritative pass on each; let scenarios add a new setting rather than repeating the rule.

issues.problem: The bold ‘Interpretation:’ label reads like an internal memo and briefly breaks magazine flow.
issues.suggestion: Fold the sentence into the paragraph without the label.
